column1: # hypothesis: Every vertex whose area-weighted normal is more than 90° from the field gradient lies on a grid edge at least one of whose incident cells straddles the crease — its eight corners do not all have the same nearer plane — so the phenomenon is two faces meeting inside one cell rather than a winding or ordering defect.
# falsified by: More than 5% of past-90° vertices whose incident cells all lie on one side of the crease
column2: which would make it a defect with a location and a fix rather than a property of one vertex per crossed edge.
